; core.fk - direct Form core stdlib.
;
; This file is executable by the current `fkwu --src` reader. The older BML
; class surface still lives at surface/core.fk as the high-grammar reference;
; this executable core keeps the same public vocabulary while carrying the
; Num/List/Cell/Task abstraction as inspectable Form data.
;
; Do not define wrappers for primitive structural operators such as head, tail,
; len, nth, cons, list, or empty here. Keeping those primitive names unshadowed
; lets source witnesses use the kernel's direct access paths.

(do
    (defn identity (x) x)

    ; The string "narrow waist" — str_len / str_byte_at / byte_to_str (plus
    ; str_concat) are the native composition floor for string behavior built in
    ; Form: measure, decompose (one raw byte, 0-255), construct (the exact
    ; dual), join. str_eq remains an orthogonal compare primitive. Confirmed
    ; present, byte-identical, on fkwu, Go,
    ; Rust, and TS (receipts/2026-07-01-narrow-waist-string-cleanup.md).
    ; Everything below is Form composition over that floor — substring,
    ; char_at, ord, int_to_str — kept as the portable fallback shape. The
    ; kernel dispatch override is intentionally narrow: byte-string/cursor
    ; waist names stay native when same-named fallback definitions are loaded,
    ; so source compilers and cursors keep byte indexing instead of accidentally
    ; routing through slower fallback string reconstruction. Other same-named
    ; Form bindings remain ordinary user definitions.

    (defn fstr-substring-loop (s i end acc)
        (if (ge i end) acc
            (fstr-substring-loop s (add i 1) end (str_concat acc (byte_to_str (str_byte_at s i))))))
    (defn substring (s start end) (fstr-substring-loop s start end ""))

    (defn char_at (s i) (substring s i (add i 1)))
    (defn ord (c) (if (eq (str_len c) 0) -1 (str_byte_at c 0)))

    ; int_to_str — decimal rendering, built from byte_to_str + arithmetic
    ; (ASCII '0' is byte 48), not a
source_tail:
it ")")) (t-splice "e"))
        (rule3 "litstr" (p-cap "v" (p-str)) (t-splice "v"))
        (rule3 "litchr" (p-cap "v" (p-char)) (t-splice "v"))
        (rule3 "litnum" (p-cap "v" (p-num)) (t-splice-int "v"))
        (rule3 "ident" (p-cap "v" (p-run "alnum")) (t-emit "ident" (list (t-splice "v"))))
        )))
)

; bml-realfiles-band.fk — point the full BML grammar at the REAL thesis files.
;
; The cursor reads each actual .bml from the master-thesis-2000 companion source,
; the BML grammar (bml.fk) matches it scannerlessly, Form objects hold the tree.
; No lexer, no stack, no Python — cursor + matching rules + Form nodes, one pass.
;
; Each file contributes one digit to the score:
;   2 = fully consumed (parse reached EOF)   1 = prefix parsed   0 = no parse
; Reading left→right (most significant first): primitive-Cut, BMF-includes,
; container-Rule, BMF-grammar. So 2222 = all four fully parse; 2000 = only the
; smallest; 2110 = smallest full, next two prefix, largest fails. Honest readout.
;
; preludes: form-stdlib/core.fk form-stdlib/json.fk form-stdlib/cache.fk form-stdlib/form-ontology-loader.fk form-stdlib/line-grammar.fk form-stdlib/bmf-core.fk form-stdlib/bmf-grammar.fk form-stdlib/bml.fk

(do
    (let SAMPLES "../docs/field/urs/artifacts/master-thesis-2000/companion/source-samples/")
    (let bg (bml-grammar))

    (defn parse-file (fname)
        (g-match-rule bg (g-start bg) (cursor-file (str_concat SAMPLES fname))))

    ;; 2 = full consume to EOF, 1 = parsed a prefix, 0 = no parse
    (defn score (res)
        (if (rok? res)
            (if (cur-eof? (skip-ws (rok-cur res))) 2 1)
            0))

    (let d-cut  (score (parse-file "primitive-Cut.bml")))
    (let d-inc  (score (parse-file "BMF-includes.bml")))
    (let d-cont (score (parse-file "container-Rule.bml")))
    (let d-gram (score (parse-file "BMF-grammar.bml")))

    ; digits, most-significant = smallest file
    (add (mul d-cut 1000) (add (mul d-inc 100) (add (mul d-cont 10) d-gram))))
